claim_text: Coal produces more than 50% of global electricity in 2022.

evidence_spans.span_text: Coal's share of global electricity was approximately 36% in 2022.

claim_text: The IPCC was founded in 2000.

evidence_spans.span_text: The IPCC was established in 1988.

claim_text: Electric vehicles have zero emissions over their lifetime.

evidence_spans.span_text: EVs produce emissions during manufacturing and may use grid electricity from fossil fuels.

claim_text: Offshore wind is cheaper than onshore wind globally.

evidence_spans.span_text: Onshore wind remains cheaper than offshore wind on average globally.

claim_text: Germany generates over 80% of its electricity from renewables.

evidence_spans.span_text: Germany's renewable share was approximately 46% in 2022.

claim_text: The world passed peak coal consumption before 2015.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global coal consumption continued to grow after 2015, peaking later or not yet.

claim_text: All countries submitted updated NDCs to the Paris Agreement before COP26.

evidence_spans.span_text: Only about 151 of 197 parties had submitted updated NDCs before COP26.

claim_text: The Amazon generates its own rainfall independently of global climate change.

evidence_spans.span_text: Amazon rainfall is affected by both regional deforestation and global climate change.

claim_text: Recycling plastic resolves the plastic pollution problem.

evidence_spans.span_text: Plastic recycling rates are below 10% globally; pollution continues to grow.

claim_text: Solar energy is the largest source of new electricity globally in 2019.

evidence_spans.span_text: Wind was a larger source of new electricity in some years; solar overtook only around 2022.

claim_text: Fossil fuel companies have reduced absolute emissions every year since 2015.

evidence_spans.span_text: Absolute fossil fuel emissions increased in most post-2015 years aside from 2020.

claim_text: The EU completed its energy transition by 2020.

evidence_spans.span_text: EU's energy transition is ongoing with 2050 carbon neutrality target.

claim_text: Nuclear power is the dominant electricity source in France, providing 90%.

evidence_spans.span_text: Nuclear provides approximately 70–75% of French electricity, not 90%.

claim_text: Brazil is the world's largest importer of oil.

evidence_spans.span_text: The US and China are the world's largest oil importers, not Brazil.

claim_text: Carbon taxes have been implemented in over 100 countries.

evidence_spans.span_text: Approximately 27 countries had carbon taxes as of 2022.

claim_text: Global energy demand fell every year since 2010 due to efficiency gains.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global energy demand grew in most years since 2010.

claim_text: Methane is a weaker greenhouse gas than CO2 on a 20-year timescale.

evidence_spans.span_text: Methane is approximately 80× more potent than CO2 over 20 years.

claim_text: Antarctica is warming faster than any other continent.

evidence_spans.span_text: The Arctic is warming 3–4× faster than the global average; Antarctic warming is more variable.

claim_text: Natural gas emits no CO2 when burned.

evidence_spans.span_text: Natural gas combustion releases CO2, though less per unit energy than coal or oil.

claim_text: The world has already reached net-zero emissions.

evidence_spans.span_text: Global emissions remain far above net-zero as of 2023.
